correctness.rationale: Symmetry, unit diagonal and [0,1] invariance are compatible with the weight field. Uniqueness preserves zero cross-block weights. Lower exponential comparison preserves any initially positive edge; the nonnegative source in the edge equation and an integrating factor then propagate positivity through paths at every positive time. In particular, an initially missing within-component pair is eligible for the critical and supercritical scalar lower comparisons. The two diagonal terms in (W²)_ij give 2w_ij; linearization of the exact edge field at zero has coefficient r=c(2+2/N)−1 with full-population N, not component size. The maximum tie sees at most (N−2)m² from off-diagonal intermediates, leaving strictly negative quadratic coefficient −4c/N at criticality. These scalar bounds give exponential decay below threshold, two-sided reciprocal bounds at the threshold, and a positive asymptotic lower bound above. Below threshold Q is integrable, giving a limit of the bounded stochastic fundamental matrix U; its determinant converges by Liouville to exp(∫tr Q)>0. Component blocks fix their constants, so an invertible block cannot map any nonconstant profile to a constant. At and above threshold one can check contraction directly: at max and min vertices of a nonsingleton component, the contribution of their mutual tie of weight at least ℓ(t), with k_i≤N, yields D⁺diam≤−2cℓ(t) diam/N. Using respectively ℓ(t)≳(1+t)⁻¹ and ℓ(t)≳1 gives polynomial and exponential decay, and the monotonic extrema give actual limits. Independently simplifying the critical maximum-edge field gives −z²[4+(N−2)z]/[2(N+1)]. Substitution of the stated two-agent w(t),d(t) gives d'=−(2/3)wd/(1+w) exactly; inverse-linear decay for the gap is nontrivial when the initial opinions differ (zero gap remains zero).
residual_risks: Conclusions are only within initial connected components, with unit self-weights and constant symmetric response. At criticality the general opinion-decay exponent is not claimed optimal.

evidence: Nugent et al. Thm. 3.1 gives existence of limits and the disjunction of vanishing opinion gap or vanishing tie. Its FOAF discussion of growing ties for coalescing opinions uses φ→1; its specific 1/2-related condition is for logistic dynamics.

Hendrickx–Tsitsiklis Thm. 1 gives convergence and equal limits in each persistent component for cut-balanced systems; under boundedness it also gives generic distinctness across different persistent components. Martin–Girard give convergence to consensus under persistent connectivity and controlled reciprocal interaction ratios.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For this symmetric W the rates are pairwise comparable since 1≤k_i≤N. Generic theorems therefore already explain qualitative consensus once a connected set of time-integrated rates diverges, including possible vanishing rates. They do not establish where this happens for FOAF, the sharp tie orders, or the uniform subcritical all-nonconstant obstruction (as opposed to generic pairwise distinctness).

evidence: The thesis explicitly observes that FOAF cannot create ties across components, and its Fig. 3.4 already depicts successive closure. Its FOAF experiments compare other response functions with network parameters. From Eq. (14) the FOAF linear coefficient is easy to obtain using diagonal self-loops, but the comparison at a maximizing tie supplies nonlinear control even when the coefficient cancels.

At the threshold the rate integrals diverge because the ties have a lower reciprocal-time bound, while below it they are integrable and give an invertible limiting opinion map. The qualitative convergence theorem does not itself give either FOAF weight bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Support closure, the local sign change, and general consensus theorems do not by themselves imply the entire global classification. Distinct content rests on the two-sided critical and off-critical tie estimates and their exact consequences, not on a generic consensus proof or isolated cutoff calculation.

value.rationale: The exact cutoff resolves whether mere positive homogeneous interaction ensures consensus in this model. Its critical regime quantifies how ties can all disappear without destroying cumulative communication, while below it the total influence never collapses a nonconstant profile. The two regimes at vanishing weights are mathematically and interpretively distinct; the result covers sparse initial graphs componentwise, not only a symmetric complete-graph trajectory.
residual_risks: Deterministic homogeneous-response restriction; not evidence for robustness to distance-dependent trust, modified normalization, or stochastic link dynamics.
